Cc: eng-team@voltadata.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff — performance priorities for Voltadata onboarding

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. To get the onboarding moving we need to align on the tuning priorities that will materially move our unit economics in month 1. High-level asks from Voltadata:

- Keep 95th P95 latency under 350ms for interactive workflows (avg prompt length ~120 tokens).
- Reduce per-query cost by at least 30% vs our current hosted endpoint by using batching / caching / quantization where safe.
- Clear fallback behavior if the dedicated pool is saturated (we need SLA-friendly routing).

Can you share a proposed implementation plan that lists the tradeoffs and gating criteria so we can get procurement and eng committed? I attached a small sample of our traffic and prompts.

Also: who from your side will own the quant profile decision and the integration checklist?

Best,
Elena
Elena Moreno
Product Manager, Voltadata

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff — performance priorities for Voltadata onboarding

Elena, thanks for the clear asks and the traffic sample — that helps a lot. High level proposal below; we'll run the details in the implementation workshop (I added a suggested agenda in the Drive link).

Quick plan (proposal):
1) Discovery (1 week) — Redwood to analyze sample traffic, token distribution, and top prompt families. Output: recommended batching window, cache prefix rules, and candidate quant profiles.
2) Safe-mode quantization A/B (2 weeks) — start with int8-symmetric on non-generation heads; validate output quality on your eval set. Gate: accuracy regression <= 1.5% on our eval metrics.
3) Cache & prefix rules (1 week) — implement KV/prefix caching for stable prompt prefixes; gate on hit-rate >= 12% and latency improvement >= 20%.
4) Batching policy (parallel) — configure adaptive batching to meet P95 target while keeping tail latency bounded.
5) Routing policy & fallback — primary dedicated pool with overflow to host API under strict rate limits; transparent metrics and cost attribution for overflow.

Owners: Redwood will own discovery and quant profile proposals (Karthik as eng owner). CS (Marissa) will own rollout communication and acceptance. You'll own final sign-off on regression gates and procurement.

Next steps: 45-minute implementation workshop — propose Wed Mar 3, 10:00am PT. I'll include a short pre-read (checklist + candidate quant profiles).

I attached the onboarding checklist and our current quant profile matrix for reference.

Cheers,
Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: onboarding_kickoff_checklist.xlsx; redwood_quant_profiles_v2.pdf

Folks — quick technical notes ahead of the workshop. I ran the sample CSV through our profiler; a few concrete observations:

- Token distribution: median 90 / 95th 210 tokens. That informs batching windows (we should target max batch size ~256 tokens equivalent).
- Prefix repetition: ~14% of requests share a stable 8–16 token prefix — good candidate for prefix KV caching.
- Model considerations: for your workload the LlamaX-7B-Quant (symmetric int8) and Falcon-7B-q4 provide the best cost-performance tradeoffs in our cluster tests.

Recommendations for the workshop:
- Bring your eval prompt set (we need concrete pass/fail thresholds to gate quantization).
- Provide expected QPS profile by route (peak and sustained). This lets us size the dedicated pool and set batch windows.
- Approve an initial safety net: any quant-induced regression above 1.5% triggers immediate rollback and routing to host API variant.

I'll prepare two candidate quant profiles (safe / aggressive) and a short script to run your eval set.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Optimization
